lower_trigram.name: Wind (Sun)
lower_trigram.nature: Subtly penetrating. Mild, nourishing. Wood and wind. The eldest daughter.

lines.image: a mat of white grass laid on the ground before the offering is set down.
lines.reading: White grass is spread on the ground before the offering is set down. You are at the start of a heavy time, and care costs little now. Put something soft under whatever you are about to carry. Let others go ahead of you, and ask for no notice. Care taken this early is what keeps the load from breaking.

lines.image: a withered willow putting out shoots, an old man taking a young wife.
lines.reading: A dry willow puts out new shoots, and an old man takes a young wife. Something you thought was finished still has life in it. The old and the new each have what the other lacks. Keep the old idea and give it a fresh shape. Everything goes well from here.

lines.image: the ridgepole bending.
lines.reading: The roof beam bends under its load. You keep pushing forward and do not know how to step back. No one can help you while you push this hard alone. Stop pressing on what is already giving way.

lines.image: the ridgepole raised, curving up and holding.
lines.reading: The roof beam is raised, and it holds. You are strong enough to carry this and humble enough to stay steady. The danger is wanting more, whether more help or more praise. Hold this load, and ask nothing more of it.

lines.image: a withered willow in flower, an old woman taking a young husband.
lines.reading: A dry willow flowers, and an old woman takes a young husband. What you have now is real, the way those flowers are, but it will not last. You are reaching for a quick fix to hold on to a strength that is fading. It earns no blame and no praise. Look instead for what will last.

lines.image: wading on until the water closes over the head.
lines.reading: You wade into the river, and the water closes over your head. You have taken on more than anyone could carry, for the sake of everyone else. Nobody else put you here, and nobody can blame you, since your reason was good. Keep going until you reach the far bank.

gene_keys.shadow:
One fear sits under every fear you have, and it is the fear of dying. Where getting through life is no longer in doubt, it changes clothes. It becomes the fear that none of it means anything. Most lives are built so that this fear never has to be looked at. It comes in three layers, and the first is the fear of living. Then comes a panic about dying some time after forty. Last comes the fear that you will die without really living. That last one is the fear that finally moves you.

Avoiding it is a dance around an empty hole, and you can dance for years. A fixed set of beliefs numbs the fear, because the mind hates surprises. Your body knows two older answers: a loving hand on your belly, and a breath that goes deeper than the fear. The body is not afraid to die. Only the fear is.
gene_keys.repressive: Turned away from their own dark side, this person lives a life with no centre. It may look glamorous or dull, but there is no juice in it. They work hard to seem happy, even to themselves. Anyone who has faced their own fears can see straight through them.
gene_keys.reactive: Here the fear turns into speed. This person takes rash risks and raises the stakes so fast that there is never a still moment to feel what drives them. They will try anything for a sense of purpose except stopping. What frightens them most is their own silence.
gene_keys.gift:
Totality is living alongside fear instead of running from it. You stay open to every change and still keep your commitments. You take in the whole of life, the pleasure with the pain, and you stop letting your mind run your days. You trust life enough to follow the story without knowing how it ends.

Life becomes a play, and you have a part in it. Lover or fool, you play your part all the way. Under the giving you find a strange calm, which is the reward for holding nothing back. Each fear you accept leaves you lighter, and hard times get a lighter touch. The demons you face turn out to be angels in disguise. As your own worries settle, your energy turns toward other people.
gene_keys.siddhi: There are moments when time stops, and in them you have no fear of death at all. The mind pictures living forever as more and more time, which is the one thing it cannot be. The present is so full that you stop waiting for the next moment. Picture the end of a great play. The actors and the crowd have gone, the lights are out, and you are still in your seat before the empty stage. That is the part of you that was there before the play began and is there after it ends. It watches, listens and breathes. It wakes through a life lived wholly, even a life wholly miserable. Near someone who lives here, your own fears come up to be seen.
gene_keys.programming_partner: Purpose looks for what the life is for and can lose sight of the people in it. Inner Majesty holds what this one lacks: the care that feeds others without asking why. Following your own purpose can look selfish, until you see it serves everyone. Open it when you are afraid that going after your purpose would be selfish.

human_design.gate: Gate 28 drives you to struggle for a life that means something. It goes toward the hard thing to find out what the struggle is for. It will change a whole life, the work or the country, to get nearer the answer. Its fear is that the road will be too hard and end in failure, so why begin. That fear can hold you still for years. A hard thing is not a failure. Lived through, it becomes a story worth telling, and other people find their own meaning in it.
human_design.centre:
The Spleen Center sits low on the left side of your body, under the ribs. It is your oldest awareness, the alertness every animal has. It reads danger through the senses in the moment, and it speaks once, quietly. It keeps you alive, so it holds your fears about staying alive, one fear to each of its seven gates. Gate 28 holds the fear that life has no point.

About 55 percent of people have this centre defined. Their alertness is steady, like a cat asleep in the sun whose ears still turn at every sound. Their risk is pushing past a warning because the body has always been strong. The other 45 percent have it open. They take in the fears of everyone around them and feel them as their own. They tend to hold on to a job or a person longer than is safe. Their gift is learning which fears are theirs.
human_design.channel: Gate 38 sits in the Root Center, the pressure at the base of your spine. It is the part of you that fights on whatever stands in the way. With Gate 28 it makes the Channel of Struggle, which tells you which fights are worth having. The fight may be for your own survival or for someone else's. Gate 38 may be in you or in someone close to you, and the struggle finds its point only when both are present.

tarot.ring_role: Purpose runs out when it waits for a later day. It belongs to the Ring of Illusion, two energies that share your fear of death. Its one sibling is UL 32, Art of Living, which carries the fear of dying before you have done what you came for. Open it when you notice you are saving your life for later.
tarot.tarot_resonance: Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.

body.physiology:
Fear is the reason this energy is given to your kidneys. They keep the store you have from birth, and a life spends it without making more. Each kidney holds about a million tiny filters, all there at birth, and no new ones are made after it. The fear that life has no point and the fear of running out are one fear, kept in one place. It stays quiet for as long as you spend the store on something that matters.

They lie high at your back, one on each side of the spine, under the last ribs. Put your hands on your waist behind you with the thumbs forward, and your fingers are over them. You will feel nothing through the muscle, though on a deep breath in they slide down a little. One kidney is enough for a whole life. You are resting your hands on the part of you that was full at birth and holds more than one life needs.
body.amino_acid: Your sense of purpose has a chemistry, and one substance in it is asparaginic acid. Your body makes it for itself from what is left when food is burned, so you never have to eat it. It is part of every protein in your body. Its share of the fear is the fear of death itself. In your body it is there when you put your life off for a later year that you hope will mean more. It is there too when you give a moment everything and feel the calm underneath. One other energy in you shares this substance and the same fear of death.

relations.unity_line: UL 27 is this card's pair and its partner at once: when you give everything to what matters, it is what keeps you fed.

pair.teaching: Purpose gives everything to what matters, and it can forget to eat while it does. Inner Majesty is where it goes next: the care that feeds whatever cannot yet feed itself. Open it when you have poured yourself out and have nothing left to give. A life given away still has to be fed.

inverse.teaching: Turn this energy end for end and it comes back the same. There is no softer side of it to run to. Whichever way you hold it, the weight sits in the middle, and so do you. Open it when you look for a way out of what you have taken on. The only way through is to stand in it.

programming_partner.teaching: Purpose looks for what the life is for and can lose sight of the people in it. Inner Majesty holds what this one lacks: the care that feeds others without asking why. Following your own purpose can look selfish, until you see it serves everyone. Open it when you are afraid that going after your purpose would be selfish.

codon_ring.name: Ring of Illusion
codon_ring.teaching: Purpose runs out when it waits for a later day. It belongs to the Ring of Illusion, two energies that share your fear of death. Its one sibling is UL 32, Art of Living, which carries the fear of dying before you have done what you came for. Open it when you notice you are saving your life for later.

tarot.teaching: Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.

sky.teaching: the sign of the sea, where your fixed edges loosen and the fear of losing yourself grows smaller.

immortals.teaching: Lake above carries Zhong Li Quan, whose fan is said to wake the dead, so what looked finished in you can live again. Wind below carries He Xian Gu, the one woman of the eight. Her lotus grows clean out of the mud, so something good can come out of a heavy time.

hebrew_letter.teaching: the letter of the Moon's night road, the part of you that goes down into sleep and meets what you fear there.

cards.essence: Commitment is a yes that rises from your belly before you have thought it through. You give it before you can see where the road leads, and from then on you are all in. It feels like a quiet warmth moving through you, with nothing nervous or loud in it. Keeping it up takes no effort, because you are letting it carry you. Your luck grows out of how whole you were at the start.

glance.reading:
Commitment is a yes that rises from your belly before you have thought it through. You give it before you can see where the road leads, and from then on you are all in. It feels like a quiet warmth moving through you, with nothing nervous or loud in it. Keeping it up takes no effort, because you are letting it carry you. Your luck grows out of how whole you were at the start.

Somewhere along the way your fears begin to ask whether you chose right, and they ask loudest when it gets hard. Let them talk, and keep going.

Give yourself to what is in front of you today, the small things as much as the large ones. Stay until the thing ends of its own accord. Each yes you follow to its end moves your life forward in a leap.

iching.trigram_combination: Water over Water is the hexagram of one hard time following another. Water is the part of you that goes into a hard thing instead of around it. Here it meets more water, because a hard time rarely comes alone. This hexagram has long been read as a stream falling from one pit into the next. You get through a hard time the same way, by going all the way into it and coming out still yourself. The same word means to repeat and to practise, so every fall makes you better at the next one. You can be deep in danger and not be lost in it.
iching.reading:
You are in trouble that does not come once. One hard thing ends and the next is already waiting underneath, so hoping it will all pass does not help. What helps is to go on the way water does, without stopping at the edge of a fall and without losing yourself in it.

So keep faith as you go on. Let everything you do come from an honest heart. Danger has its use as well. A river and a wall keep a city safe, and there is a time to use a hard place the same way.

Your heart does the work now. Tie it to what you know is true, and keep moving.
judgement_lines: Danger, repeated. If you are sincere, your heart gets through.
Whatever you do from there is worth doing.
image_lines: Water flows on and on and reaches where it is going: danger, repeated.
So the wise keep to what is right, day after day, and teach by doing it again.

upper_trigram.name: Water (K'an)
upper_trigram.nature: Precipice, dangerous place. Stream, flowing water, river. Venture and fall. The middle son.

lower_trigram.name: Water (K'an)
lower_trigram.nature: Precipice, dangerous place. Stream, flowing water, river. Venture and fall. The middle son.

lines.image: in the pit, going down into a hole in its floor.
lines.reading: Already in danger, you go down into a hole in the floor of the pit. That is what happens when you repeat a mistake you have already seen. Losing your way at the start is innocent. Keeping to it once you know is what digs the hole. Change course now, and a late success is still a success.

lines.image: danger in the pit; seeking small things, and getting them.
lines.reading: The danger is all around you, and you have not sunk far. You cannot get out yet, but you can gain a little. Seek small things, one foothold at a time. The way out is made of steps that size.

lines.image: coming or going, a pit either way.
lines.reading: Every way you turn there is another pit, forward or back. Each move you make takes you deeper in. When a situation overwhelms you, it is human to turn frantic, and the wise stay calm. Hold still and do nothing for now. The time to act will come, and it is not yet.

lines.image: a jug of wine and a bowl of rice in plain clay, passed in through a window.
lines.reading: A jug of wine and a bowl of rice, in plain clay, passed in through a window instead of the door. At the worst of it, simple and honest is enough. Bring what you have, plainly, to someone who can help you. In the end there is no blame.

lines.image: the water level with the rim, not spilling over.
lines.reading: The water has risen level with the rim and does not spill. You are close to solid ground, and what was rough is being made even. Level here also means at peace. Do not try to fill it higher. Stay level, and you will come out.

lines.image: tied with cords, set in a thicket of thorns, three years without the way.
lines.reading: Tied with cords and set down among thorns, you find no way out for three years. The cords are ones you tied yourself, by keeping to what was doing you harm. Three years is the price of refusing to change. Find someone who has found the way out, and follow them.

gene_keys.shadow:
Half-heartedness is a yes with one part of you kept back. You go into the work or the relationship, and a part of you stays on the bank, in case. From inside it feels like good sense. It is a quiet dishonesty with yourself, and your days go dull or turn into one upset after another. You picture how life should go, and when it does not match, your energy pulls out of the present and runs ahead in your head.

You give up at the first sign of trouble, or you cannot stop doing what hurts you. Under both is a fear you have never gone into. Leave a stretch of life before its natural end and the same pattern comes back, with different people, until you finish it. Looking back, you can see the loop, and that is how it teaches you.
gene_keys.repressive: This person keeps every promise, even after the thing it was made for has ended. They cannot tell when something is over, so they take on more than they can carry. They wear themselves out and let other people use them. They do not dare to say that it should end.
gene_keys.reactive: Here is someone who says yes to everything and pulls out when the pressure comes. They talk things up and cannot deliver. What sets them off is someone else expecting something of them. Each broken promise leaves them with disappointment and shame.
gene_keys.gift:
Commitment runs like a great river from deep inside you out into what you do. You cannot force it or will it, any more than you can force trust. With it you do not need to think about the goal, because the goal is already inside the decision. Only time shows where the river goes. Your life is made of cycles inside cycles, some five minutes long and some a lifetime. Each one gets the same whole yes, from the way you make love to the way you wash the dishes.

A commitment like this lasts as long as it lasts. When it is over, both of you feel it at the same time, and what began cleanly ends cleanly. Its length has nothing to do with success or failure. Held whole, it rides out any storm. It is not about the other person, but about leaping with your eyes open.
gene_keys.siddhi: Devotion is commitment gone mad: you leave the order of your mind for the wildness of your heart. Everyone is devoted to something already. A mother is devoted to her children, and even someone in despair to their misery. At first the love pours toward one thing, a person or a cause, and people call it blind. Then the love you poured out starts pouring back from everything, until even the rocks and trees seem to bleed it toward you. It is nearly impossible to say no to someone who lives like this. The heart they follow keeps no rules. To be devoted is to lie forever in the lap of what you love.
gene_keys.programming_partner: This yes stays through a cycle, and desire is what starts the cycle. Sparking the Blaze holds that desire, the want that draws two people together in the first place. Every desire runs for its own length, a day or a year, and followed honestly it shows you how long. Open it when you cannot tell whether a wish deserves your yes.

human_design.gate: Gate 29 sits in the Sacral Center, low in your belly. It presses you to give your energy to what you said yes to, and to stay. It says yes easily. Every yes and every no carries weight, because each one shapes the years that follow. A yes from your body carries you through setbacks, and people learn they can rely on you. A yes from your head, or one said out of fear of saying no, traps you in something you have no energy for. Then devotion turns into obligation. Look at what you said yes to without meaning it, and get out of what you can.
human_design.centre:
The Sacral Center sits under the navel and above the legs, and it is the strongest engine you have. It is the energy to work, to make things, to raise a child and to stay with anything for years. It does not decide. It answers with a sound that rises before you have thought, a yes that lifts or a no that goes flat. It answers only what is actually in front of you, never a question you asked yourself in your head.

In about seven people in ten this engine runs all the time. When they act on a real yes the energy renews itself, and when they work without one it burns out. In the other three the engine is open. It takes in the energy around it and can outwork everyone for a while, but it does not know when enough is enough. Its gift is the pause. Every drive seated here passes through the first excitement, the jump in and then a plateau where nothing moves. Whether you are finished or only paused, this place can tell you, if you ask it for a yes or a no.
human_design.channel: Gate 46 sits in the G Center, the centre of who you are and where your life is going. It carries the love of being in a body. With Gate 29 it makes the Channel of Discovery, the energy to commit to life as you live it. It puts you in the right place at the right time, and it turns ordinary moments into full ones. The channel runs only when both gates are present, in you or in a person you are with.

tarot.ring_role: This yes is the part of love that stays. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Union, whose theme is how people come together. UL 4, Veils of Knowledge, carries a love that needs no reasons. UL 7, Essential Nexus, carries the guidance that comes from being truly together. UL 59, Mystics Treasures, carries the longing for union with another. This one carries the yes given with all of you.
tarot.tarot_resonance: The ring and the doubled water bring three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.

body.physiology:
Your body answers before your mind does, which is why this energy is given to the weave of nerves at the base of your spine. The engine that does your work is seated here, and its yes comes before any thought. That yes is the only one your body will keep. Say yes from your head to something it had no energy for, and it is your body that pays. The low back is also where the will is kept, the part of you that keeps going after the yes is given.

Put a hand flat at the base of your back, on the flat bone between the two dimples. The weave lies just inside it. From there it stands you up from a chair and keeps your hips level as you walk, without you watching. Your hand is resting on the part of you that goes on.
body.amino_acid:
The yes you give with all of you has a substance in you, and it is valine. It goes into every protein you build, tucked deep inside, away from the water around it. Your body cannot make it, so it has to come from food such as meat, eggs or beans.

What you hold back from someone you love is held in this chemistry too, deeper than words. There, keeping back one part in a hundred is the same as keeping back almost all. The same substance runs through three other energies of love and closeness. Together they are changing what commitment means, away from what others expect and toward a yes to life itself.

relations.unity_line: Read alongside Sparking the Blaze and a family of four, this is how a yes, a desire and a bond between people come together.

pair.teaching: This yes goes all the way in, and it meets itself whichever way it turns. Its hexagram is one of the eight that come back the same when turned over. Going in or coming out, the danger is the same, and so is what gets you through it. There is no other side to escape to, only the next low place to fill.

inverse.teaching: This yes goes all the way in, and it meets itself whichever way it turns. Its hexagram is one of the eight that come back the same when turned over. Going in or coming out, the danger is the same, and so is what gets you through it. There is no other side to escape to, only the next low place to fill.

programming_partner.teaching: This yes stays through a cycle, and desire is what starts the cycle. Sparking the Blaze holds that desire, the want that draws two people together in the first place. Every desire runs for its own length, a day or a year, and followed honestly it shows you how long. Open it when you cannot tell whether a wish deserves your yes.

codon_ring.name: Codon Ring of Union
codon_ring.teaching: This yes is the part of love that stays. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Union, whose theme is how people come together. UL 4, Veils of Knowledge, carries a love that needs no reasons. UL 7, Essential Nexus, carries the guidance that comes from being truly together. UL 59, Mystics Treasures, carries the longing for union with another. This one carries the yes given with all of you.

tarot.teaching: The ring and the doubled water bring three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.

sky.teaching: the twins, two lives held as one, as two people are when each gives the other a whole yes.

immortals.teaching: Both trigrams are water, so one figure stands above and below. He is Li Tie Guai, the healer who came back from his own death carrying medicine in a gourd. He went all the way into the worst that can happen and came back with something that heals. That is the road a full yes can take you down.

hebrew_letter.teaching: a blade makes one clean cut, the way a real decision ends your wavering and sets you on one road.

cards.essence: Passion is alive in you as heat, and you feel it first in your stomach. When something catches you, your whole body leans toward it. A spark is enough to set you blazing. Your wants make your days bright. People are drawn to that warmth, and your passion wakes theirs.

glance.reading:
Passion is alive in you as heat, and you feel it first in your stomach. When something catches you, your whole body leans toward it. A spark is enough to set you blazing. Your wants make your days bright. People are drawn to that warmth, and your passion wakes theirs.

Some wants take hold, and your mind fans them the way wind fans a flame. Your body needs food and sleep, but most wants are for things you could live without. In the heat of it, a want feels like a need. Sometimes you follow one to the end and find it cost more than it gave. Forgive yourself, because you needed to learn it.

Feel every want all the way, and follow the few that matter most. A want is neither holy nor wicked, so there is nothing to feel guilty about. You can enjoy the pull of it and still know it will pass. Held like this, passion stops weighing on you, and you move through your days lighter.

iching.trigram_combination: Fire over Fire is the hexagram of what your light holds on to. Fire below is the warmth in you, the part that feels and wants. Fire above is the clarity in you, the part that sees what is worth wanting. The seeing sits above the wanting because a flame lasts only as long as what it burns. Fire has long been read as clinging, since a flame has no shape of its own. It takes the shape of the wood it is on. What you hold on to is what your light becomes.
iching.reading:
Something has lit you up, and the question is what you are holding on to. Everything that shines or grows holds to something, the sun to the sky and the grain to the ground. Your fire lasts only as long as what it burns. Hold to what is true, and your light goes a long way.

What it asks is gentleness with your own strength. The old counsel is to raise a cow, and like a cow you can be strong without pushing. Tend the light in you before you spend it. No fire burns without fuel, and yours comes from the people and the world around you. So stay close to them.

Your heart is where this fire is kept. Light it first, and let its warmth reach the people nearest you. From there it reaches the four corners of the world.
judgement_lines: The clinging fire. It is good to hold to what is right, and it goes well.
Raise a cow, and there is good fortune.
image_lines: Brightness rises twice: this is fire.
So the great keep the light going, and it reaches the four corners of the world.

upper_trigram.name: Fire (Li)
upper_trigram.nature: Glowing light spreading in all directions. The power of consciousness. Magical fire-bird. The middle daughter.

lower_trigram.name: Fire (Li)
lower_trigram.nature: Glowing light spreading in all directions. The power of consciousness. Magical fire-bird. The middle daughter.

lines.image: footprints crossing every way at the start.
lines.reading: The footprints run every way at the start, because you are eager and do not yet know the road. You want to use your light before you have learned to tend it. You have not lost anything yet. Slow down and take each step with care, and no blame comes of it.

lines.image: yellow light, the colour of the middle.
lines.reading: Yellow light is the light of the middle, softer than the glare of noon. You know you cannot see it all, and you let others show you what they see. That openness is what makes you strong. Keep to the middle, and the fortune is as good as it gets.

lines.image: the sun going down, and a jar to drum on.
lines.reading: The afternoon sun is going down, and no light stays at its height. You can drum on a jar and sing, or you can mourn the years going by. Fear of the ending is what turns this hour bad. Take the evening as an evening, and sing while the light lasts.

lines.image: it comes all at once, flames up, dies down and is thrown out.
lines.reading: A want comes over you all at once, flares up, dies down and is thrown aside. You leapt at it with nothing to feed it, so it burns hot and finds no place to stay. Do not wait until you burn out to see that a flare is not a fire. So come slowly.

lines.image: tears in floods, and a sigh of grief; then good fortune.
lines.reading: Tears come in floods, with sighing and grief, and good fortune follows. You have seen that you are not as bright as you thought. While you weep you do nothing rash, and your pride goes out with the tears. Feel the pain of others as your own. Keep your place, and let the grief do its work.

lines.image: the king marches out; he strikes the leader and spares the followers.
lines.reading: The king marches out, strikes the leader and lets the followers go. In you, the leader is the one want that drives all the others. Take that one on, and leave the small passing thoughts alone, since they only followed. Aim at the head and spare the rest, and there is no blame.

gene_keys.shadow:
Desire is a hunger that has left the stomach and gone out into the world. It is a hunger for experience itself, for every taste there is, the bitter ones too. It is not for anything in particular. You are built to yearn, and what you reach for is never the point. The moment you are full, you are empty again, and the yearning starts over.

The suffering comes from what you do against it. Fight the wanting and it grows. Call it unholy and it grows faster. So most people neither give in nor let go, because both are too frightening, and they live half-heartedly in between. The fire itself is not the trouble. The war with it is.
gene_keys.repressive: Pushed down, the wanting takes the life force down with it. The whole person stiffens, in body, feeling and mind. Life turns into a serious business, with rules laid over every appetite. Under the rules is a fear of being burned by what they feel.
gene_keys.reactive: Let loose, the wanting follows every want without care and scorns every rule. When the world disapproves, they throw themselves further in. They mean to end the wanting by wearing it out. It wears them out first, often young.
gene_keys.gift:
Lightness comes when you stop fighting and say to life: all right, do your worst. What gives way then is your distrust, the sense that life is against you. You see the joke, that things had to go the way they went, and you see your own place in the story. From then on there is a glint in your eye.

Wants still come and go. Each one is a guest you ask in for tea, and it either leaves in its own time or stays until it is followed. Either way, you know no want will bring you lasting peace, so it has lost its hold. You laugh at yourself first. Real lightness is never afraid of being swept away by a feeling.
gene_keys.siddhi:
Rapture is the one longing left when all the others have burned down into it. Under the thousands of wants that pass through you each day, one grows stronger. It is the longing to be free of suffering and to go back to where you came from. Step into it willingly, and you give up everything, even the wish to be free. You become your longing, and in that you feel you belong in the world.

Then bliss burns you, over and over. It is so close to the surface that whoever comes near you is likely to catch it.
gene_keys.programming_partner: This fire pulls you toward the next promise, and at its edge it leaves every road half walked. All In holds what it lacks, the yes that commits and stays the course. Open it when you keep starting things and dropping them for something new. You feel light once you know you are committed.

human_design.gate:
Gate 30 sits in the belly and carries the wish to feel everything, together with the fear of feeling it. It is the most intense gate there is, and it turns up whatever else you carry. It drives you toward a dream you can feel, strong enough to live by. You can hold that dream a long time and bring it into form.

The risk is burnout, and it is often learned young, from leaping the moment the heat rises. So the drive asks you to know which dream is worth the fuel. Wait for the right time to share it. Fed by devotion, a passion lasts for years. Keep your own flame, and it stays lit for the long road.
human_design.centre:
The Emotional Solar Plexus Center sits in the belly, and it is where feelings are made. It is the only centre that both drives you and lets you know things. It moves in a wave, from hope down to disappointment and up again. The wave is chemistry, and a single feeling lasts only a few minutes unless you hold on to it. There is no truth at the top or the bottom of the wave, so a real decision waits until it has passed.

A little more than half of people have this centre defined, and their feelings are with them all the time. For them the work is to watch the wave rather than become it: anger is rising, rather than I am angry. The rest have it open. Other people's feelings come in and grow louder, then fade when those people leave the room. Being nice can become a way to keep those feelings off. Lived well, an open centre is empathy, knowing what someone feels as if it were yours.
human_design.channel: Gate 41, at the base of the spine, is the pressure to imagine an experience before it happens. With Gate 30 it makes the Channel of Recognition, a dream joined to the feeling that can live it. This channel waits to be recognised and invited before it acts. Its low comes when what you hoped for does not arrive, and the bottom falls out of your world. Gate 41 may be in you or in a person close by, and a dream catches fire only when both are there.

tarot.ring_role: This fire burns off what it feeds on, and it cannot do the burning alone. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Purification, and the other is Universal Crest. There, the force of wanting meets the ability to listen to what the past has taught. Open it when your wanting keeps making the same mistake.
tarot.tarot_resonance: Three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, come to this energy through its ring and its two fires.

body.physiology:
Your body gives this energy to the solar plexus, and the reason is hunger. The solar plexus is a knot of nerves behind your stomach, the largest of its kind. Its fibres run out in every direction like the rays of a sun. In front of it is the soft hollow under your breastbone, the pit of the stomach. Miss a meal by an hour, and the pang arrives right there, whether you meant to eat or not. Your fear arrives in the same place. So your body feels a want before you have decided anything about it.

Lay a hand flat in that hollow and take a sharp breath in. It pushes out against your hand, then falls back as you let the breath go. About a hand's depth behind your palm is the part of you that wants first.
body.amino_acid:
When you give in to a strong want, it runs through you like a fire, and your body feels it first. That fire has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is glutamine. Your body makes it for itself, in your muscles. Your body builds its proteins from twenty small pieces, and your blood carries more of this one than of any other. It carries what is left of a burnt protein safely out of the muscle to where it can be let go.

Follow every want and you often feel low afterwards, and part of that low is this chemistry. The same substance is in you when you listen as when you burn. Your fire burns to make you clean. As your longing grows stronger, your body begins to fill with light.

relations.unity_line: Each of these is somewhere your wanting can go next: deep into water, into a promise kept, into listening.

pair.teaching: This fire rises and spreads its light outward, and it has no depth of its own. All In is where it goes next: water that drops into the deepest place and keeps going. Open it when you have been lit up by many things and given yourself to none of them.

inverse.teaching: This fire looks the same from every side, and turning it around shows you nothing new. Face your wanting from any direction and you meet the same fire. There is no other side of it to escape to.

programming_partner.teaching: This fire pulls you toward the next promise, and at its edge it leaves every road half walked. All In holds what it lacks, the yes that commits and stays the course. Open it when you keep starting things and dropping them for something new. You feel light once you know you are committed.

codon_ring.name: Codon Ring of Purification
codon_ring.teaching: This fire burns off what it feeds on, and it cannot do the burning alone. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Purification, and the other is Universal Crest. There, the force of wanting meets the ability to listen to what the past has taught. Open it when your wanting keeps making the same mistake.

tarot.teaching: Three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, come to this energy through its ring and its two fires.

sky.teaching: the goat's sign, slow and steady on a long climb. It comes here through the Devil, and for you it means a fire kept burning evenly.

immortals.teaching: Both fires carry Lu Dong Bin, a scholar with a sword. The old stories say he used it to cut through his own cravings. For you he is the part that can cut a want loose when it has held on too long.

hebrew_letter.teaching: the letter whose name means eye. It comes by the same route, and it asks you to look plainly at what holds you.

cards.essence: Sometimes everyone in a room feels the same thing, and nobody says it. You sense it before anyone speaks. When you say it, they recognise what they felt and could not put into words. You have no wish to lead, and that is why they trust you.

glance.reading:
Sometimes everyone in a room feels the same thing, and nobody says it. You sense it before anyone speaks. When you say it, they recognise what they felt and could not put into words. You have no wish to lead, and that is why they trust you.

Some days you speak to be seen, and the words go hollow. When you notice it, stop talking and listen again. Then ask what would help the people in front of you.

Listen before you speak. Let people see you make mistakes, because they follow the most human person in the room. Choose each word with care, because words go on working long after they are said. Said at the right moment, one plain sentence of yours can turn a whole room.

iching.trigram_combination: Lake over Mountain is the hexagram of two people drawn to each other. Lake is the part of you that opens up, smiles and answers. Mountain is the part of you that stays still and does not reach. The openness rests on the stillness because only someone who is not grabbing can be moved. This hexagram has long been read as a lake on top of a mountain. A proud peak holds no water, but a hollow at the top holds a whole lake. It works the same way between you and a crowd. Let people move you, and you will move them.
iching.reading:
You and someone else are drawn to each other, and neither of you has moved yet. The other side may be a person, or a piece of work that has caught hold of you. What this time asks is that you receive rather than reach. Chase someone and they back away. Stay open and still, and they come to you in their own time. Give more than you are given, and you end up with more.

Every attraction has a strain in it, and that strain carries the feeling across. Once you know the feeling is true, commit to it. What you put in is what you get back.

Your body feels it first, as a stir that climbs from your toes to your mouth. Stand still with your face open, and let what is coming come to you.
judgement_lines: Influence. It gets through, and it grows. It goes well for the one who stays true.
Taking a young woman as a wife brings good fortune.
image_lines: A lake on top of the mountain: that is influence.
So the wise keep room in themselves, and people come to them.

upper_trigram.name: Lake (Tui)
upper_trigram.nature: Open surface, interaction, pleasure, the mouth, exchange. The youngest daughter.

lower_trigram.name: Mountain (Ken)
lower_trigram.nature: Limit, frontier, stillness. Solid, steady, unshakable. The youngest son.

lines.image: a stirring in the big toe.
lines.reading: The feeling stirs in your big toe, and a toe can move but cannot walk. Something outside you has caught your attention. It is too early to tell whether it will come to anything. Notice it, and take no step on it yet.

lines.image: a stirring in the calves, and staying put brings good fortune.
lines.reading: The feeling moves into your calves, which cannot walk on their own and only follow the feet. You want to go before anything has carried you. Going now would go badly. Stay where you are until the time to move comes to you.

lines.image: a stirring in the thighs, holding on to those it follows.
lines.reading: The feeling reaches your thighs, and you hold on to the person walking ahead of you. Following someone into being who you are not will shame you. What you cling to here is beneath you. Stay who you are, and let the people behind you follow you.

lines.image: the heart unsettled, going and coming, and only friends follow its thoughts.
lines.reading: This line is the heart, where a feeling is decided. Hold it steady and good fortune comes, with nothing to regret. If your mind goes back and forth, only the friends you already have will follow your thoughts. Settle your heart, and what you feel will reach further than the people you know.

lines.image: a stirring in the flesh of the back, above the heart, with nothing to regret.
lines.reading: The feeling reaches the flesh of your back, close to the heart but not in it. Nothing selfish moves you here. Something you cannot see is moving you, as you move others. Leave room in yourself for a change of heart, and you will have nothing to regret.

lines.image: a stirring in the jaws, the cheeks and the tongue.
lines.reading: At the top the feeling reaches only your jaws and tongue. What comes out can be tireless teaching or sweet talk that is not true. Talk alone does not move anyone for long. Do what you have been saying.

gene_keys.shadow:
The need to be recognised grows out of feeling unsure of yourself. The less sure you are, the more you look to others to tell you who you are. One kind is loud: the one who knows best and makes sure you know it. The bully is always the least sure person in the room. Another kind is quiet and harder to spot, the calm certainty of having found the right way while others have not. Both hold on to the words and lose the feeling behind them.

The strange thing is that you cannot see it in yourself. Look for it and the part of you doing the looking is the part that hides it. It shows only when you fall in front of people. Sooner or later life arranges that fall for everyone.
gene_keys.repressive: This person hands their power to anyone close by and places themselves below. They care deeply what others think and fear above all being called proud. Their modesty is worn where it can be seen, so it draws the notice it claims not to want. Under it is fear.
gene_keys.reactive: Here the pride is open, and it runs on anger. Such a person sees how easily others are led and looks down on them for it. They miss how much they need those same people to notice them. Praise from people you look down on never feels like enough, so the scorn keeps growing.
gene_keys.gift:
Being followed happens to people who are not looking for it. You have an ear for what people are about to feel, and you can say it in words they understand. What moves them is the feeling behind the words. A thing said at the right time reaches much further than what it says.

You use what you know about how people are led to lead them out of traps you were once caught in. To speak for what is new, you first learn the language of what came before. It asks for patience with your own mistakes. It asks for the quieter courage to stay with what you know is true while people misread you. You will fall where everyone can see, and you get up with your heart still open. That is what people follow.
gene_keys.siddhi:
What anyone thinks of you stops mattering, and nothing about it is gentle. A soft voice and a lowered head are often pride in disguise. This comes when life has stripped you to the bone and you stopped minding. You would not even mind being thought proud. You leave the world as it is.

You say what has to be said, knowing the words came from everyone and go back to everyone. Where they land is not your concern. You fell where everyone could see, and this time you stayed down. It is quiet down here. From the ground you can look up and laugh.
gene_keys.programming_partner: This energy gives words to what is new, and it has nothing to say until the new thing arrives. Beginning and the End holds what it lacks: the picture of a better life before it has a shape. One sees the future and the other says it out loud. Whatever is new meets resistance at first, and the two face it together. Open it when you are asked to speak and nothing new has come to you.

human_design.gate:
Gate 31 sits in the throat and presses you to speak for a group. It says what the group has felt and not yet said. It works only when you are called into it. Take it for yourself and the voice loses its power. The moment your own wanting steps in front of the group, people stop hearing you.

From outside this can look like ambition or like hiding. It fails in two ways: pushing forward to be approved of, or shrinking back for fear of not being heard. Called, it listens first, and people follow what you heard in them.
human_design.centre:
The Throat Center is where what is inside you comes out as words or as action. Every other part of you is pressing to reach it. It has no power of its own. It works like a gearbox, and whatever part of you is joined to it does the talking. Through this gate it reaches the centre of the chest, the part of you that knows who you are. So what comes out is you, and a harsh word about it lands on you and not on your idea. The mind writes a careful script, then the voice says something else.

About seven people in ten have this centre defined. Their voice is steady, the same tune every time, and it carries. It goes out more easily than it takes in, and it is heard best at the right time. The other three have it open. They take in every voice in the room and feel the pressure to talk without knowing what to say. Words come before the thought, sometimes as a blurt. Left quiet until they are invited, they can speak for the whole room.
human_design.channel: On its own, this voice needs something to steer it. Gate 7, in the centre of the chest, knows which way a group should go. Together the two make the Channel of the Alpha, the leader the people choose. The direction comes from the chest and the words from the throat, looking ahead to what could work better. Gate 7 may be in you or in a person close by, and the group is led only when both are present.

tarot.ring_role: This energy moves people with words, and it cannot take back what it says. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of No Return, whose theme is words that cannot be unsaid. Its one kin is UL 62, Voice of Nature, which finds the exact word for you. This one gives you the word that turns a room.
tarot.tarot_resonance: Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, show this energy in faces you may already know.

body.physiology:
This energy is given to your throat, and the reason is the air. Your voice is air taken from the room and sent back into it through two closed folds, with your shape on it. The shape is the only part that is yours. It is the one thing your body makes that reaches inside another person across a room. That is what influence is in the body: something taken in and given back. When your throat is easy, the words go out on the breath. When it is tight, you are pushing air, and people hear the push.

Say a long sentence out loud and notice where it stops. It stops where the breath ran out. You cannot say a word on the breath in. What you say is made from what you took in first.
body.amino_acid:
When you speak from the heart, the words come out in order before you have thought about what they mean. That has a substance in you, and the substance is tyrosine. It is one of the twenty your body is built from. Your body makes it from another one you must eat, and meat, eggs and beans carry it too. From it your body makes what wakes you up and gets you moving, and the colour of your skin, hair and eyes. The sentence that leaves you before you choose it is made from the same substance as the colour of your eyes.

The word that forms in your head when you look at a tree runs on this substance too. So do the words you follow and the words you lead with. Cut an apple and leave it on the table, and it turns brown. A close relative of what made your colour does the browning. It goes on working in the open air, as a word does once it has left you.

relations.unity_line: UL 32 is this card's pair and its inverse at once: the long stay, where this one is the first pull.

pair.teaching: This energy is the first attraction between people, and it runs out when the newness fades. Art of Living is where it goes next: the sense of what will last, which keeps a bond alive after the first thrill. Open it when the early feeling has gone and you want to stay. What starts by drawing people in lasts only if it is kept.

inverse.teaching: Turn this energy end for end and the first pull becomes the long stay. Art of Living is the same bond seen years later. Open it when you are asking whether something will last.

programming_partner.teaching: This energy gives words to what is new, and it has nothing to say until the new thing arrives. Beginning and the End holds what it lacks: the picture of a better life before it has a shape. One sees the future and the other says it out loud. Whatever is new meets resistance at first, and the two face it together. Open it when you are asked to speak and nothing new has come to you.

codon_ring.name: Codon Ring of No Return
codon_ring.teaching: This energy moves people with words, and it cannot take back what it says. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of No Return, whose theme is words that cannot be unsaid. Its one kin is UL 62, Voice of Nature, which finds the exact word for you. This one gives you the word that turns a room.

tarot.teaching: Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, show this energy in faces you may already know.

sky.teaching: the heat that catches and spreads, as a word spreads from one person through a crowd.

immortals.teaching: Lake above carries Zhong Li Quan, the old general who left his army and whose fan is said to bring the dead back to life. Mountain below carries Zhang Guo Lao, the hermit who rides his donkey facing backward. One gave up command and the other keeps his eyes on where he has been. Both show you a way to lead without taking charge.

hebrew_letter.teaching: the letter of fire, whose sound is breath pushed through the teeth, the edge every word you speak passes over.

cards.essence: When the newness of something has worn off, the long middle begins. A feeling for what will last comes alive in you here. You can tell which plans and friendships have a future in them before you could say why. You know what to keep and what to let go.

glance.reading:
When the newness of something has worn off, the long middle begins. A feeling for what will last comes alive in you here. You can tell which plans and friendships have a future in them before you could say why. You know what to keep and what to let go.

Some days a quiet panic runs under everything. You rush from one task to the next toward a rest that never comes, and underneath it is the fear of failing. Slow down inside the rush, and it loosens its grip. An ending met with grace is never a failure.

This is the art of living: to take your time with things and enjoy more of your days. Let people in, even when it hurts, because being opened is what makes you rich. Ask what you want to leave behind, and give your days to that. Lived this way, an ordinary life becomes something worth handing on.

iching.trigram_combination: Thunder over Wind is the hexagram of lasting, of how a thing goes on once it has begun. Thunder is the part of you that stirs things up and acts where others can see. Wind is the part of you that works quietly underneath and never stops. The stirring sits on top because what lasts needs action on the outside and patience within. Thunder and wind have long been read as a couple married for years. One of the two makes the moves the world sees, while the other keeps the home going. Your life lasts the way the seasons do, by changing as it goes. What lasts in you is one bold part and one patient part working together.
iching.reading:
You are in something for the long haul now. The start is behind you, and what matters is how you keep it going. You may be carrying more than was ever fairly yours. The way to bear it is to keep changing inside while you stand firm on the outside.

Bear the hard days with dignity, and the good ones with humility. Change yourself, and leave others to change in their own time, since forcing it on someone is oppressive. Look for allies who are least like you, because a bond between different people holds the longest. Keep a direction, since it helps to have somewhere to go.

Your legs do the work now: the feet that carry you forward and the thighs that bear the weight. Stand the way someone stands through a long day, with feet planted and knees soft.
judgement_lines: Lasting. It goes well, and there is no blame.
It pays to hold steady. It helps to have somewhere to go.
image_lines: Thunder and wind: the picture of lasting.
So the wise stand firm and do not change direction.

upper_trigram.name: Thunder (Chen)
upper_trigram.nature: Arousing power emerging from the depth of the earth. Excite, influence, move, affect. The eldest son.

lower_trigram.name: Wind (Sun)
lower_trigram.nature: Subtly penetrating. Mild, nourishing. Wood and wind. The eldest daughter.

lines.image: digging for depth at the very start.
lines.reading: You dig for depth on the first day, wanting the settled form of a thing before it has grown one. Forcing yourself to last is not lasting. Push now and nothing you try will help. Let the thing find its own pace, even when that feels like losing control.

lines.image: regret gone, in the middle ground.
lines.reading: Your regret goes as you find the middle ground. You are neither too keen nor unwilling, and you hold to your way rather than to any one thing on it. You have more strength than you show. Use only as much as the moment needs, and you will have nothing to regret.

lines.image: a start that never reaches its end.
lines.reading: You set your heart on something and then drop it, keen one day and gone the next. People notice, and even when you are right it shames you. A start that never reaches its end earns no one's trust. Live by the rules you ask of others before you go on.

lines.image: a field with no game in it.
lines.reading: You are hunting a field with no game in it. However hard or cleverly you try, there is nothing there to catch. The effort is real, and the place is wrong. Stop moving about, go back to where you belong, and be still there.

lines.image: one way kept from start to finish.
lines.reading: You stay faithful to one way from start to finish. For someone who follows, that is right and it holds. For someone who has to decide, the same steadiness is a fault, because deciding means changing with what comes. Know which part is yours before you keep to it.

lines.image: restlessness kept up at the top.
lines.reading: You keep yourself stirred up long after the force has run out. You feel full while you are empty, raised high and close to a fall. Restlessness kept up for years achieves nothing. Choose one long road and commit to it, then stop wearing yourself out on motion.

gene_keys.shadow:
Failing, deep in the body, means being cut off. Long before you, the people you come from learned that to be pushed out of the group was to die. That lesson is still in you. Today the fear has moved into money. The bigger the number, the safer you feel. Yet it never settles, because fear always needs something to feed on. Take the money away and it would find the next thing. Close beside it is the fear that your family line will end, with no one to hand anything to.

The fear made people stingy in spirit, keeping to their own small circle, and it kept the species alive while it did. It lives deep in the body, and the mind feeds it by telling its story again. Let go into the way life moves, and you find the support was there all along.
gene_keys.repressive: This person pulls in tight. The rules are held so hard they cut, and everyone outside the circle is suspect. They are choking themselves in body, in feeling and in money, starved of breath and of help. Groups made this way stop meeting the wider world, and in time they die out.
gene_keys.reactive: Here the thread of a life has been dropped. Underneath is anger that nothing holds them up but themselves, and it drives one bad decision after another. Each decision cuts them off a little further from what could support them. Their days have no rhythm, and nothing they start lasts.
gene_keys.gift:
Keeping things alive is what this energy becomes, and its whole art is choosing which things deserve to go on. You sense the long run of a situation. You can hold your energy or your money back from what tempts you but would not serve. You trust a feeling about someone that no reason supports, and it proves right. The balance is between holding back and taking a chance. The one who buries his coin for fear of losing it loses it.

The craft is grafting. You keep the old rootstock, the part that has proved strong, and set the young shoot onto it. Then one day you see that what you fought to preserve was never the real thing, and its shell cracks. You can plant a few trees every day around your home, lose most of them, and keep planting through wars and changes of government. In time you stand in a forest where the ground was bare, with villages living off it. Whether or not anyone learns your name, you will know.
gene_keys.siddhi: Reverence is what remains once the fear has burned away. You see your place in the long chain of living things, with lives behind you and lives still to come. You look at it with no self in the way, so all that is left is wonder. You stand on the shoulders of those who came before, and you offer your shoulders to whoever comes next. Even the smallest insect is holding you up. You feel tiny and huge in the same breath. Wisdom lives in one person for a while, then moves on to the next who can hold it. The one discipline it asks is to pause and listen inward.
gene_keys.programming_partner: This energy knows what to keep, and it can hold on too long. Moving to Perfection holds what it lacks: the ease of letting a thing end so the next has room. Between the two is the whole breath of a life, keeping and releasing. Open it when holding on has started to cost more than it gives.

human_design.gate:
Gate 32 is a sense of what will last, and it sits in the Spleen Center. It reads a plan, a job or a friendship for whether it has a future, and it usually knows before you could explain. Growth under it comes in cycles rather than leaps, because real change takes time. The drive is to prepare, to set the stage so you are ready when the moment comes, without dragging it closer.

The fear of failing presses from the same place. It can stop you from trying at all, or from preparing, so you are not ready when the time is right. It can also push you too hard, too fast, for too long. The line to find is between holding on and clinging.
human_design.centre:
The Spleen Center is the body's oldest awareness, the alertness that keeps you safe and well without a word. It works through the senses. It is the centre of time, telling you in each moment whether to move. It also holds the survival fears. Gate 32's fear is the one that says: I might fail, so I will not try.

About 55 in 100 people have this centre defined. For them the hunch comes steadily, speaks once and softly, and does not repeat. The risk is letting the mind talk over it. Followed, it keeps the body well. The other 45 in 100 have it open. Time tends to slip for them, and they take in the fears of the people around them as if they were their own. They also tend to hold on to jobs and relationships longer than is good for them. What they have instead is a fine sense of what is healthy for someone else, and their best decisions are slow ones.
human_design.channel: Gate 32 can tell which big dreams to follow, but it has no push of its own. Gate 54 sits in the Root Center at the base of the body. It is ambition, the drive to rise from where you started. Together they make the Channel of Transformation, which picks the right dream and sees it through, in work or in waking up. Gate 54 may be in you or in someone close to you, and the dream moves only when both are present.

tarot.ring_role: This energy keeps a life going, and under it lies an old fear of dying before that life has been lived. It belongs with one other card in the Ring of Illusion, whose theme is the fears that look solid until you face them. UL 28, Becoming the Mystery, carries the fear of death itself. This one carries the fear of failing to live well.
tarot.tarot_resonance: Five of the tarot's major cards arrive through the ring and the two trigrams, each a turn your life can take.

body.physiology:
Keeping is the reason this energy is given to the spleen. Your blood passes through it many times a day, and it sorts what it finds. It retires what is worn out and keeps what still serves. A red cell lives about four months, and most of them end here, taken apart. Their iron is kept and sent back to be built into new cells, so your body loses almost none of it. The red in your blood today was carried by cells long gone. In the old medicine the spleen holds the blood inside its vessels and moves the water through you. It also turns what you eat into what you live on.

It sits high under your left ribs, behind the stomach, about the size of a fist. Look at the pink under your fingernails. That colour is iron your spleen has kept for you, cell after cell, for years.
body.amino_acid:
Keeping what matters has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is asparaginic acid. The letters your body is written in are partly built from it. Joined to one other piece, it is the sweetener printed on a can of diet drink. In a body that keeps and counts, the fear of death and the worry about money run together, older than any bank account.

What is yours in it is the fear of dying with your life unlived. The same chemistry holds the old root and the young shoot, what has lasted for generations with the new set onto it. You share this chemistry with one other energy, the one that fears the ending itself.

relations.unity_line: UL 31 is this card's pair and its inverse: the pull that begins a bond, where this one keeps it going through the years.

pair.teaching: This energy keeps a bond going through the years, and it runs thin when the pull that started it is forgotten. Theater of Truth is where it goes next: the attraction that draws two people together in the first place. Open it when something long-lasting has gone flat and needs its spark again. Anything that lasts starts with a pull.

inverse.teaching: Turn this energy over and the long marriage becomes the first meeting. Theater of Truth is the same bond seen from its start, when one person moved another. Open it when you have forgotten why you began.

programming_partner.teaching: This energy knows what to keep, and it can hold on too long. Moving to Perfection holds what it lacks: the ease of letting a thing end so the next has room. Between the two is the whole breath of a life, keeping and releasing. Open it when holding on has started to cost more than it gives.

codon_ring.name: Ring of Illusion
codon_ring.teaching: This energy keeps a life going, and under it lies an old fear of dying before that life has been lived. It belongs with one other card in the Ring of Illusion, whose theme is the fears that look solid until you face them. UL 28, Becoming the Mystery, carries the fear of death itself. This one carries the fear of failing to live well.

tarot.teaching: Five of the tarot's major cards arrive through the ring and the two trigrams, each a turn your life can take.

sky.teaching: the last sign of the year, where one cycle dissolves into the next and your old patterns loosen.

immortals.teaching: Thunder above carries Cao Guojiu, the nobleman who left the court and its riches. He is the part of you that can walk away from comfort to live truer. Wind below carries He Xian Gu, who chose a simple life in the mountains. She is the part of you that needs little to keep going. Between them, what lasts in you is a way of living, not the things you own.

hebrew_letter.teaching: the part of you below waking thought, where the old patterns of a life are kept.

cards.essence: After anything big, you need time on your own to look back at it. Mindfulness is alive in you here: you go over it quietly until you can see what it was about. Even your mistakes have something to teach you once you see them from a distance.

glance.reading:
After anything big, you need time on your own to look back at it. Mindfulness is alive in you here: you go over it quietly until you can see what it was about. Even your mistakes have something to teach you once you see them from a distance.

The hard part is the pace of life, with the next thing always coming at you, so the days go by without a second look. The people near you may read your quiet as distance. Take the time anyway, let the bad hours go, and forgive yourself for them.

Give part of every day to what has just gone by, even if it is only a cup of tea drunk slowly. Ask what was best about yesterday and let yourself feel it again. Talk it over with a friend, and you will both feel closer. Wait to tell your story until it can lift the person who hears it. Then what you have lived becomes something you can give.

iching.trigram_combination: Heaven over Mountain is the hexagram of knowing when to step back. Heaven is the strength in you that keeps moving forward. Mountain is the part of you that knows where to stop. The stopping sits below the strength because a strength that never stops wears itself out. This hexagram has long been read as a mountain under a sky that is drawing away. A person who leaves in good time takes all of their strength with them. It is a time when something smaller has begun to gain ground, the way the days shorten after midsummer. You keep what matters by stepping back before you are pushed.
iching.reading:
Something smaller than you has been gaining ground for a while, and arguing will not stop it. Staying to fight spends your strength on ground that is already going. So leave while leaving is still your choice. This is not running away. You decide how far and how fast, and you go with what is yours.

Keep your distance from what is small, and do not hate it, because hating would tie you to it. Be firm, and carry no bitterness out the door. In small things, keep doing what is right. Knowing when to step back is the hardest call there is. A step back at the right hour often turns out to be the way forward.

In the body this is the head and the hand. The hand below has put the work down, and the head above stays clear. Let the hand rest, keep your head up, and go.
judgement_lines: Retreat, and it goes well.
In small things, it still pays to hold firm.
image_lines: A mountain under heaven: that is retreat.
So the wise keep small-minded people at a distance, without anger, with reserve.

upper_trigram.name: Heaven (Ch'ien)
upper_trigram.nature: Unceasing forward movement, dynamic, enduring, untiring. Spirit power. Heaven, sovereign, father.

lower_trigram.name: Mountain (Ken)
lower_trigram.nature: Limit, frontier, stillness. Solid, steady, unshakable. The youngest son.

lines.image: the tail of the retreat, and danger.
lines.reading: You are the last one out, with the danger close behind. Any sudden move now only draws it on. When a tiger comes, the deer at the back of the herd lives by stepping aside and standing still while the rush goes past. Make no move in any direction yet.

lines.image: held fast with a strap of yellow ox hide, which no one can loosen.
lines.reading: You have made up your mind to go, and it holds like a strap of ox hide that no hand can loosen. Keep quiet inside, so nothing from outside gets in and nothing of yours slips out. Praise and money cannot move you now. The outcome is not known yet, so hold to what you have decided.

lines.image: a retreat that is tied, dragging its sickness after it.
lines.reading: You want to go, and you are held by people too close and too familiar to leave. The strain wears you down, and nothing large can be done from here. You can still look after the household that depends on you. Do that much well, and let the great work wait.

lines.image: a willing retreat, made in spite of what you love.
lines.reading: You are leaving something you love, and you go of your own free will. That is the whole test, and small-minded people cannot pass it. Store your strength while what threatens it is still small. Guard your life as carefully as you would guard a jewel, and go.

lines.image: an admirable retreat, made at its proper hour.
lines.reading: The work is done, and you step down before anyone asks you to. You could stay and take more, and you choose not to. You have gifts to spare, and you keep them quiet. Hold to what is good, and do not let anything false spoil what is real. Leave while it can still be done well.

lines.image: a rich retreat, and nothing left to doubt.
lines.reading: You leave with all you brought in. Nobody can hold you back or bend you now. No part of you is pulling the other way, so there is no doubt left. You have lost none of it, inside or out. Go gladly, because everything is working in your favour.

gene_keys.shadow:
Forgetting is how a life goes when there is never a pause in it. Your eyes stay on what is coming, the next message or the next job. You rarely look at where you have just been. So you walk through the forest head down and cross each clearing without stopping. You miss what was waiting there, a sunrise or a stranger. The same argument comes round again, and each time it feels new. Life starts to feel hard in a way you cannot name.

The memories you carry keep you in the pattern, and every wish you have seems to add another. One wish loosens it: the wish to remember who you are. The people you cannot get free of help you most, the ones you feel you have known from somewhere, loved and fought with in turns. Stay with them, and they wake you up. Everyone forgets in this way, even though forgetting leaves each person feeling separate and alone.
gene_keys.repressive: This person has gone into hiding. They find it hard to talk to anyone and cannot break out of their own silence. They hide in their work or a strict routine, far from other people or in a kind of numbness. When they finally wake, the wisdom they have taken in surprises everyone, themselves included.
gene_keys.reactive: Anger drives this one, and so does a fear of feeling alone. They point out other people's faults, often calling it help, until they get the angry reaction they wanted. The resentment builds until it bursts. Once they stop putting their rage on other people, they remember what it is to love and be loved.
gene_keys.gift:
Mindfulness starts the day you catch yourself in the middle of a heated argument and see that you have forgotten who you are. You still hide or react, and now you can watch yourself doing it. For a while that is harder than sleeping, because now you feel every repeat. The patterns seem to grow stronger the nearer you come to the end of them. They are not stronger; you are more awake. Nothing you do can hurry this, and the watching is all you can lean on.

Then the trees open into a clearing. There is light and a place to sit, and from there you can see the path you have been walking. Sit down in it for a while. From here you can make something out of what you feel, because you can see it without drowning in it. Your best work happens when you are out of its way.
gene_keys.siddhi:
Revelation comes to you as silence, the way autumn comes to a forest. Your life turns brighter as it lets go, the way leaves do before they fall, and your attention turns inward. All that you were is forgotten, and all that you could be is remembered. The past no longer stands between you and this moment. Here you have no more to tell, and if you speak at all, it is to say that.

Your story is coming to its end. Part of you does not want it to end, and the greater part is ready to let go. Fall in love with your own story and follow it without holding anything back. It will reach its end, and no one else's will be like it.
gene_keys.programming_partner: This energy needs time alone, and alone it can forget the people who wake it up. Solection holds what it lacks: the pull toward the people you need and who need you. The two meet in your closest relationships, the hard ones most of all, where old patterns come up to be seen. Open it when you have been on your own long enough and someone is waiting for you.

human_design.gate: Gate 33 sits in the throat and pushes you to step back from the world after something has happened. You go off alone to go over it and gather your thoughts, and this is not hiding. Then you come back and share what you found, with a depth you could not have had before. The people near you may take the distance for coldness, so say plainly that you need the time. Its risk is going over the past too long, alone, until it turns to worry. When it runs well, your story lifts whoever hears it. When it runs badly, you tell a story of pain that keeps you and your listener stuck where you were.
human_design.centre:
The Throat Center sits in your neck and is where what is inside you comes out, as words or as action. Energy from all over you rushes toward it. It is the meeting place through which you reach other people.

About seven people in ten have this centre defined. Their voice is always there for them, whether or not they use it, with one steady tone that others know them by. The other three have it open. As children they were often not heard, so some went quiet and some got louder. They can feel pressure to speak without knowing what to say. Their gift is to meet each person in the tone that person needs, and to say what a whole room is feeling. They speak best when someone asks.
human_design.channel: Stepping back has nothing to go over until something has been taken in. Gate 13 sits in the centre of the chest and is the listener, the part of you that collects other people's stories. Together they make the Channel of the Prodigal, which takes life in and keeps it until the time is right to share it. It works in silence first and is not built for small talk. Gate 13 may be in you or in a person close by, and the channel runs only when both are present.

tarot.ring_role: This energy looks back, and looking back is where waking up begins. It belongs to a family of three, the Ring of Trials, whose theme is the tests on the way to knowing who you are. UL 56, Infinite Journey, carries the test of being pulled away by your senses. UL 12, Petals of Freedom, carries the last test of meeting who you really are. This one carries the first: seeing that you have forgotten.
tarot.tarot_resonance: Four of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.

body.physiology:
This energy is given to your throat because you hear your own voice from inside. Everyone else hears your voice through the air. You hear it by a second road as well, through the bones of your own head, which carry the low notes best. So the voice you have heard all your life is the one from within. A recording of it sounds thin and high, like a stranger's. Your life is the same: only you have heard it from inside. A gland below your voice stores two to three months of what it makes, so what runs you today was made a while ago.

Block both ears with your fingers and say a few words. Your voice sounds louder and deeper, because the road through the air is shut and only the one through the bone is left. What you hear then is the part of your voice that nobody else has ever heard.
body.amino_acid:
No substance in you answers to this energy. It is a mark in the code you are written in, one of three that name nothing. Where your body's reading reaches it, the reading stops. The written message runs on past it, and only the reading ends there. When these marks come alive in you, they begin to unplug you from the world your senses show. Past every stop in you, another beginning is written further on. Something starts where you come to an end.

This energy is the first of three such stops in you. Only the strength of your own dissatisfaction can shake you out of sleep, and it begins at this first stop.

relations.unity_line: UL 34 is this card's pair and its inverse at once: the strength that pushes forward, where this one steps back.

pair.teaching: This energy steps back to look at what happened, and it runs out once the looking is done and something has to be acted on. Sublime Power is where it goes next: the full strength that pours in when something real calls for it. Open it when you have understood the past and it is time to move. What you gathered alone is spent in the world.

inverse.teaching: Turn this energy end for end and stepping back becomes pressing forward. Sublime Power is the same strength seen from the side that advances. Open it when you have rested long enough and the time to act has come back.

programming_partner.teaching: This energy needs time alone, and alone it can forget the people who wake it up. Solection holds what it lacks: the pull toward the people you need and who need you. The two meet in your closest relationships, the hard ones most of all, where old patterns come up to be seen. Open it when you have been on your own long enough and someone is waiting for you.

codon_ring.name: Ring of Trials
codon_ring.teaching: This energy looks back, and looking back is where waking up begins. It belongs to a family of three, the Ring of Trials, whose theme is the tests on the way to knowing who you are. UL 56, Infinite Journey, carries the test of being pulled away by your senses.
